text:
Alex: Heads-up — hitting a wave of preemptible evictions in us-west1 this morning, ~23 in the last hour. A couple of user streams got cut mid-token. We should standardize a runtime pattern to avoid truncated user responses.

Maya: Logs? any commonalities (instance type, kernel, preemption window)?

Sam: Pushed a quick grep: most are n1-preemptibles and preemption notice window is shorter than expected (some ~15s). Streaming handler waits to finish current token then flushes, which loses partial token if shutdown hits during emit.

Jordan: We should implement a token-bridging handshake + resume_token flow. High level proposal: on SIGTERM, runtime enters DRAINING, snapshot last_n_tokens + minimal KV, send a handshake to a fallback runner with a small blob, then switch client stream to new endpoint with resume_token. If handshake fails, fallback to request requeue.

Sam: Sketch of the handshake (pseudo):
```
# on preempt notice (15s)
drain_window = 8s
state = DRAINING
snapshot = { last_tokens, kv_digest }
POST /handoff -> { snapshot }
# if 200 -> send resume_token to client; cutover
# if 500 -> requeue request to queue with backoff
```

Li: Main risk is KV cache rewarm cost. Suggest we store a compact cache dump (KV keys + small topo) to objectstore during drain and let fallback pull only keys present in snapshot. That keeps cold start CPU minimal. Also ensure we TTL snapshots so we don't leak memory.

Maya: Also need to avoid thundering herd on requeue. If many in-flight streams requeue simultaneously we can saturate the queue. Use client-side reconnect jitter + server-side rate limiter. Example: exponential backoff with capped jitter and token-bucket per-model.

Alex: For streaming UX, clients need a simple contract. Proposed header semantics: when cutover is possible, runtime returns a "Resume-Token" and a short-lived cutover endpoint. Client reconnect flow: open new stream with header `Resume-Token: <hex>` and `Cutover: true`. Server will validate token and resume from last_token + continue. If token invalid, return 410 -> client retries full request.

Maya: Example reconnect HTTP:
```
POST /v1/streams/resume
Headers: 
  Authorization: Bearer ...
  Resume-Token: ab12cd34
Body: { client_id, session_id }
```
Response 200 => stream resumes; 410 => client restarts request.

evict-bot: Scheduled preemption notice: instance gce-p-vm-42 will be preempted in 90s (notice_id=px-20240328-004)

Jordan: Drafting a lightweight state machine for runtime:
- RUNNING
- PREEMPT_NOTICE_RECEIVED -> enter DRAINING (start snapshot + send handoff request)
- HANDOFF_PENDING -> WAIT_HANDSHAKE (timeout 6s)
  - success -> CUTOVER (emit resume_token to client, redirect)
  - failure -> ENQUEUE_RETRY (requeue request)
- SHUTDOWN
Make timeouts conservative: prefer handing off to local dedicated pool in same region first, then cross-region fallbacks.

Sam: Also add metrics: handoff_attempts, handoff_success_rate, avg_handoff_latency, resumetoken_accept_rate, requeue_rate, rewarm_seconds. We'll use them on the runtime dashboard and alert when requeue_rate > 1% over 5m.

Li: Implementation notes: snapshot should be O(1) cost relative to tokens (we only serialize last 64 tokens + kv_digest). Don't attempt full model checkpoint. Use compressed msgpack and store to ephemeral objectstore with short TTL.

Alex: Action items:
- Jordan: PR runtime state machine + resume_token header + metric hooks (canary target: tomorrow 09:00 PST)
- Sam: Add server-side requeue throttler + queue-awareness to prefer nearby dedicated capacity
- Li: Implement compact cache snapshot + ephemeral pull API for fallback runners
- Maya: Update client SDKs to accept Resume-Token flow and fallback jitter logic

Maya: +1 :thumbsup:

Sam: I'll add a simulation job to the chaos harness to force preempt notices during streaming to validate handoff windows and requeue limits.

Alex: Good. If we can keep drain snapshot <8s and handshake <4s we should avoid most user-facing truncations. Let's sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow at 08:30 PT for rollout plan.

Jordan: Will open the PR and link the design doc.

Li: I'll prototype the snapshot serializer today and push a demo to the canary branch.

Alex: Thanks everyone.
